config.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year

personas.name: Monica
personas.goals: A budget that funds something for every grade
personas.hidden_agenda: Promised the band director she'd fight for instruments

personas.name: Kwame
personas.goals: Never spend the carryover to zero
personas.hidden_agenda: Got burned two years ago when a fundraiser flopped

personas.name: Lisa
personas.hidden_agenda: Half the trumpets are held together with tape

personas.name: Arjun
personas.goals: Spend where it helps the most kids
personas.hidden_agenda: Thinks the trip subsidy is regressive
catchphrases: if you look at the numbers

pack.title: PTSA budget planning - next school year

agenda.title: Revenue plan
agenda.goal: Decide on dues and fundraisers for next year

agenda.title: Budget process
agenda.goal: Agree the timeline to the membership vote

beats.summary: What came in and went out; Arjun's carryover number is too rosy
Dues, fundraisers and Monica's membership guess
Instruments vs the science fair vs the trip; the eighth-grade count gets fixed
Timeline to the vote; a date mix-up corrected

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Alrighty, let's start with where we ended up this year. Kwame, the headline?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Per the books, income was thirty-one four, expenses twenty-nine eight.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: So, if you look at the numbers, we're carrying over something like fifteen thousand.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Carefully. It's nine thousand one hundred. The rest was already committed to the library fund.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Ah. Right, the library fund. I forgot that moved.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: Nine thousand. Okay. That's less than I hoped.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: What did spirit wear bring in? It felt like a good year.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Thirty-two hundred profit. Best year yet.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: The hoodies. Every kid has the hoodie.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Quick thought, should spirit wear just become a bigger part of the plan?

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Maybe. Let's hold that for revenue.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: And the district matched two thousand, which we should not count on again.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Why not?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Per the district, it was a one-time pilot.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Alrighty. So we start next year with nine one and no guarantee of the match.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: I'll be honest, that's a sobering start.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: So here's my thinking. Dues are fifteen dollars, and we have about four hundred families.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Should we raise dues? Twenty dollars wouldn't kill anyone.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: It would kill some families. Some of our kids are on free lunch.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Carefully. Raising dues usually drops membership. We saw that at the elementary school.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Then dues stay at fifteen. I don't want to price anyone out.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Then spirit wear is the lever. If you look at the numbers, it's our best margin.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: A second spirit wear sale in the spring? The kids would love it.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: The vendor has a minimum order. We'd need to check.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: I can look into the vendor minimums, if nobody else wants it.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Would you? That'd be great.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Sure. I'll get the vendor's minimums and pricing by next week.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: Quick question, what happened to the restaurant nights? They used to be fun.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Did everyone see the new crosswalk on Birch? It finally has a light.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: About time. I've been honking at that intersection for years.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: The crossing guard brought cookies to celebrate.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: So, the fun run. Are we doing it again?

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Yes, the fun run stays. It's half our income.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Agreed.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Requests. Lisa, you go first. I know you're dying to.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: I'll be honest, the band needs instruments. The request is seventy-five hundred.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: That's most of our carryover.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: It's ten years of trumpets that are held together with tape.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: And the science fair is nineteen hundred, same as always.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: And the eighth-grade trip subsidy. Forty dollars a kid.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: If you look at the numbers, two hundred eighth graders at forty is eight thousand.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: It's two twenty-eight next year. It's a big class.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Two twenty-eight. So, over nine thousand.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Carefully. We cannot fund all three in full.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: So here's my thinking. Science fair in full, instruments in full, trip subsidy cut in half.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Quick thought, what if the trip subsidy only goes to families who need it?

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: The kids would know who got it. Kids always know.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Not if it's done quietly through the counselor.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: That could work. It also costs a lot less.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Alrighty. Science fair in full, instruments in full, and the trip subsidy goes need-based through the counselor. That's what we're proposing.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: The trumpets thank you. I'll get three quotes for the instruments before the vote.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Somebody should probably talk to the counselor before we put that in writing.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Last thing. The vote is May fourth, right?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Per the books, it's the fourteenth. May fourteenth.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Fourteenth. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: When does the draft go out to members?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Two weeks before. Carefully, so people have time to read it.

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: I'll write the cover letter explaining the need-based subsidy, so nobody's surprised.

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.text: Should I bring a trumpet to the vote? For drama?

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Absolutely bring the trumpet.

turns.speaker: Arjun
turns.text: Who's presenting the numbers at the vote?

turns.speaker: Monica
turns.text: Alrighty, I think we're done. Thank you, everyone.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Goodnight.
